title: OPTIMA: Design-Space Exploration of Discharge-Based In-SRAM Computing: Quantifying Energy-Accuracy Trade-offs
problem: Circuit nonlinearities and PVT variations pose major challenges in designing robust in-SRAM computing accelerators. These physical constraints make it difficult to achieve reliable computation while maintaining energy efficiency.
motivation: In-SRAM computing promises significant energy efficiency gains, but addressing design challenges is critical for practical accelerator deployment.
method: OPTIMA is a computer program that quickly predicts how much power a math operation uses inside specialized computer memory (6T-SRAM—a type of memory chip built from six transistors). When multiplication happens in this memory, electrical charge flows along thin wires called bitlines; OPTIMA mathematically models this flow to determine energy use and calculation accuracy. It runs about 100 times faster than traditional detailed circuit simulations while maintaining accuracy within 0.88 mV RMS error, letting designers quickly test thousands of different circuit designs. The tool finds which configurations best balance energy consumption against calculation accuracy, especially for neural networks that use reduced-precision numbers (quantized DNNs) to classify images and patterns.
key_novelty: The main innovation is a fast computational model that predicts power consumption and calculation accuracy in SRAM-based arithmetic, replacing detailed simulations and enabling engineers to rapidly test thousands of circuit designs.
contributions: OPTIMA modeling framework for analyzing bitline discharge and power consumption in 6T-SRAM-based accelerators
~100x simulation speed-up with 0.88 mV RMS modeling error for in-SRAM multiplications
Optimized multiplier design achieving 1.05 pJ energy per 4-bit operation
Demonstrated quantized DNN classification: 71.8% (ImageNet top-1), 90.4% (ImageNet top-5), 92.5% (CIFAR-10)
primary_theme: energy-efficient in-SRAM computing design through circuit modeling
